issue_context.title: Add `frozen_default` parameter on `dataclass_transform`
issue_context.body:
# Feature or enhancement

Add a new `frozen_default` parameter to [`dataclass_transform`](https://peps.python.org/pep-0681/#dataclass-transform-parameters) similar to the existing `eq_default` and `order_default` parameters.

# Pitch

- Frozen dataclasses are very popular when working with Jax (`flax.struct.dataclass` and `tjax.dataclass`), so being able to indicate that they are frozen by default would improve the user experience.
- `dataclass_transform` is currently supported by Pyright/Pylance and Pyre. Both teams are in favor of implementing this new parameter. Since `dataclass_transform` supports kwargs for experimentation/extensibility, Pyright was already able to [add support](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/commit/bedc124c394f01bbdea79809953ceb0299d42a7b) for `frozen_default`.
- All feedback on typing-sig has been in favor of this enhancement.

# Previous discussion

Discussed in [typing-sig](https://mail.python.org/archives/list/typing-sig@python.org/thread/IKZULRE5UZVIN7B6IMFR2CXIF6RYIJ2O/).

review_comments:
I think `frozen_default` should be `True` here.
Because we define `class CustomerModel(Decorated, frozen=True):`, we should pass `frozen_default=True` to `dataclass_transform` in this specific case.

PEP 681 says:

> At runtime, the `dataclass_transform` decorator’s only effect is to set an attribute named `__dataclass_transform__` on the decorated function or class to support introspection. The value of the attribute should be a dict mapping the names of the `dataclass_transform` parameters to their values.

I would therefore expect the `Decorated` type to have a `__dataclass_transform__` attribute, but not `CustomerModel`, and therefore I would not expect the `frozen=True` on `CustomerModel` to have any effect on `__dataclass_transform__`.

Sorry, I was not clear enough :)

I interpreted this test case as "we test frozen things" here. And I tought it might a good fit to use `frozen_default=True` on `Decorated` here as well.

But, on the other hand: passing `frozen=True` might indicate the opposite that `frozen_default` is indeed `False`.

Oh, I see. If we want to verify that `frozen_default` is `True` in `__dataclass_transform__` when it should be, how about if I set `frozen_default=True` in `test_metaclass`? It's the only test where `frozen` isn't used. We could also add a test specifically to test `__dataclass_transform__`.
